title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a sheet from Grothendieck's preparatory notes on 'Complexes de De Rham à puissances divisées' (cote 136). The paper is recycled: it is the verso of a typed page, p. 120 of SGA 7 Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §9.7, the monodromy pairing). That typescript shows through the sheet. The so-called NEXT PAGE transcription is that typescript, not a continuation of these notes.

The handwritten mathematics, in modern terms:
(1) Data.
- k is a commutative ring.
- S is a coassociative, counital, cocommutative k-coalgebra, with comultiplication S -> S ⊗_k S (boxed in the top margin).
- Hence V_k(S): k' ↦ S^{k'} = Hom_k(S, k') is a functor from commutative k-algebras to commutative unital rings (convolution product). That is, V_k(S) is an O_k-algebra in the category of affine k-schemes: a 'ring scheme', the linear dual or Cartier-dual viewpoint.
- \bar S ⊂ S is a sub-coalgebra. Restriction gives a homomorphism of O_k-algebras V_k(S) -> V_k(\bar S).
- S^+ = S/\bar S is the quotient module. Since Δ(\bar S) ⊂ \bar S ⊗ \bar S, the composite S -> S⊗S -> S^+⊗S^+ factors through S^+. So S^+ is a coassociative, cocommutative, non-counital coalgebra.
- Dually, S^{+k'} = Ker(S^{k'} -> \bar S^{k'}) is an ideal. So V_k(S^+) = V_k(S)^+ is an Ideal in the ring-scheme V_k(S).
(2) A divided-power structure γ on the pair (S, S^+).
- By definition this is a PD structure γ_i : V_k(S^+) -> V_k(S^+), i ≥ 1, on the ideal-scheme.
- Since V_k(M) = Spec Sym_k(M), the γ_i are morphisms of k-schemes. Equivalently they are algebra maps γ_i^*: Sym_k(S^+) -> Sym_k(S^+).
- By homogeneity of degree i, these are equivalently k-linear maps γ_i^*: S^+ -> Sym^i_k(S^+), subject to the dualized PD axioms ('conditions évidentes').
(3) A k-linear t : S^+ -> k, i.e. a k-valued point t of the PD ideal V_k(S)^+(k).
(4) Announced construction. From (S, \bar S, γ, t) one defines a simplicial object in the category of functors from commutative k-algebras to commutative graded (alternating) differential algebras with PD ideals. Equivalently it is a simplicial affine k-scheme in homogeneous DG-algebras with differential of degree +1, with PD ideals, the divided powers compatible with the grading and the differential.

Purpose: a 'representable', coalgebra-dual and functorial model of the PD de Rham complex, a basic object of crystalline cohomology. A PD ring-scheme with a section t presumably plays the role of a PD polynomial or PD-envelope coordinate; the simplicial direction is probably a Čech/bar-type nerve built from the comultiplication. The page stops before the construction is given.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The non-counital coalgebra structure on S^+ = S/\bar S is legitimate because \bar S is a sub-coalgebra (Δ(\bar S) ⊂ \bar S⊗\bar S), even though the quotient by a sub-coalgebra is not a coalgebra quotient in the usual (coideal) sense.
Gap: the PD axioms dualized to linear maps S^+ -> Sym^i(S^+) are not written out ('conditions évidentes').
Gap: the simplicial object itself (its terms and face maps) is announced but not constructed on this page.

ideas.what: Represent ring-valued functors by coalgebras: k' ↦ Hom_k(S,k') for a cocommutative coalgebra S, with sub-coalgebras giving quotient homomorphisms and kernels giving Ideals
ideas.modern_name: Linear dual / Cartier-type duality between cocommutative coalgebras and (formal) affine ring schemes; O-algebras in a topos
ideas.where_published: Related O-module/ring-object formalism in SGA 3 Exp. I and EGA; this exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Divided-power structure on an ideal-scheme encoded by linear maps γ_i^*: S^+ -> Sym^i_k(S^+)
ideas.modern_name: PD structure on a ring scheme / dual description of divided powers (Γ vs Sym duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1954-55) for divided powers; Berthelot (1974) for PD structures in crystalline cohomology; Roby for Γ
ideas.where_published: Not as such; PD formalism appears in Grothendieck's 1966 letter/IHES talk 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Simplicial object in functors to PD commutative DG-algebras, attached to a PD ring scheme and a section t
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial / Čech–Alexander model of the PD de Rham complex; PD dg-algebras (Cartan); precursor of derived/simplicial de Rham constructions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent, derived de Rham, 1971-72); Berthelot–Ogus; later Bhatt (derived de Rham, 2012)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a coalgebra-dual, scheme-theoretic framework: ring schemes V_k(S) with a PD Ideal V_k(S)^+ given by linear maps S^+ -> Sym^i(S^+), plus a point t. From this he announces a simplicial object of PD-DG-algebra-valued affine schemes, i.e. a representable model for PD de Rham complexes. The construction is left unfinished on this page.
missed.quote: Alors on définit un objet simplicial dans la cat. des foncteurs (k-alg comm.) → (algèbres graduées alternées différentielles (diff. de degré 1) avec idéaux à puiss. divisées
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The approach treats PD de Rham complexes as representable functors and simplicial objects in PD-CDGA schemes. This is close in spirit to later Čech–Alexander and derived de Rham descriptions of crystalline and prismatic cohomology. One would need the rest of cote 136 to judge whether it contains anything beyond those.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a setup page in standard formalism: coalgebra duals, PD structures on ideal-schemes. It is interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's c. 1975-76 representable approach to PD de Rham complexes, but nothing here is finished or clearly absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Top box: '[S ↦ S⊗_k S]' should read 'S → S ⊗_k S' (the comultiplication).
The 'NEXT PAGE' text (SGA 7 IX p.120, monodromy pairing) is the typescript on the verso, visible by show-through. It is not part of these notes.
'V_k(\bar S): fait une O_k-Alg.' should read 'V_k(\bar S) est une O_k-Alg. ass. unit. comm.'
'défini par des hom. de k-...[?]' is probably 'défini par des hom. de k-sch.' (morphisms of k-schemes).
'γ_i^*: Sym_k(S^+) → Sym^i_k(S^+)' is probably 'Sym_k(S^+) → Sym_k(S^+)' (algebra maps), followed by 'ou de hom. lin.'
'(ou, en vertu des calculs dont en fait' is likely '(ou, en vertu des calculs, sont en fait'.
'avec des conditions de [?]' should read 'avec des conditions évidentes'.
'k = dans la cat. des schémas affines' should read 'i.e. dans la cat. des schémas affines'.
Final line: 'compatibles avec graduations et [?] dérivations différentielles' is probably 'compatibles avec graduations et opérations différentielles'.
